raw_response:
I am getting older, so on these 6 mu I do not want to toss around too much. We have only 2 people in the house, and wheat-maize is what I know best. I have done this for many years, and around here everybody follows this rotation because it is steady. I will keep all 6 mu in wheat first, then after harvest turn it straight into summer maize. I do not want to gamble on fancy seed or too much extra input. If I spend too little, the crop will show it fast, especially wheat in spring. If I spend too much, the money is tied up and pumping water also costs money. So I will do about what worked before: wheat gets base fertilizer plus one topdress, and maize gets one base and one chasing fertilizer if the stand looks good. Water I will use carefully from the well, mainly at the key stages, because without watering at the right time the yield can fall badly here.

For wheat, I will sow in early October, not too early, not too late, using a common improved variety people around here plant. I usually like the field prepared simply after maize, with rotary tillage if I can arrange it. I will put fertilizer under before sowing, then add more around jointing if the wheat color is not strong enough. Wheat needs more watching through winter and spring, and I will irrigate around overwintering, jointing, and maybe grain filling depending on rain. After wheat harvest in June, the time is tight, so maize has to go in quickly. I do not want much tillage then, just quick residue clearing and direct or shallow planting so I do not miss soil moisture. Maize I will keep simple too: hybrid seed, enough fertilizer to hold the yield, one or two irrigations only if rain is short. If insects or weeds show up, I will spray, but I do not spray for no reason. This way the land stays in the system I trust, and the money stays within what a small household like mine can carry.
